audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 9, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Jonathan covenant memory, Mephibosheth's disability, dynastic fear, land restoration, compulsory court residence, Ziba's household labor, and demeaning self-language.

verses.restored: David said, Is anyone still left from house of Saul, that I may do covenant-kindness with him for Jonathan's sake?

familiar.text: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?

modern.text: Then David asked, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד הֲכִ֣י יֶשׁ ע֔וֹד אֲשֶׁ֥ר נוֹתַ֖ר לְבֵ֣ית שָׁא֑וּל וְאֶעֱשֶׂ֤ה עִמּוֹ֙ חֶ֔סֶד בַּעֲב֖וּר יְהוֹנָתָֽן

verses.restored: There was a servant from Saul's house named Ziba. They called him to David, and king said, Are you Ziba? He said, Your servant.

familiar.text: And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba. And when they had called him unto David, the king said unto him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.

modern.text: And there was a servant of Saul’s family named Ziba. They summoned him to David, and the king inquired, “Are you Ziba?” “I am your servant,” he replied.

original.text: וּלְבֵ֨ית שָׁא֥וּל עֶ֨בֶד֙ וּשְׁמ֣וֹ צִיבָ֔א וַיִּקְרְאוּ ל֖וֹ אֶל דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אֵלָ֛יו הַאַתָּ֥ה צִיבָ֖א וַיֹּ֥אמֶר עַבְדֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: King said, Is there no one still from house of Saul, that I may do kindness of Divine with him? Ziba said, Jonathan still has a son, injured in both feet.

familiar.text: And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, which is lame on his feet.

modern.text: So the king asked, “Is there anyone left of Saul’s family to whom I can show the kindness of God?” Ziba answered, “There is still Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הַאֶ֨פֶס ע֥וֹד אִישׁ֙ לְבֵ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וְאֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה עִמּ֖וֹ חֶ֣סֶד אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ ע֛וֹד בֵּ֥ן לִיהוֹנָתָ֖ן נְכֵ֥ה רַגְלָֽיִם

verses.restored: King said, Where is he? Ziba said, Look, he is at house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.

familiar.text: And the king said unto him, Where is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lodebar.

modern.text: “Where is he?” replied the king. And Ziba said, “Indeed, he is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir son of Ammiel.”

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמֶר ל֥וֹ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֵיפֹ֣ה ה֑וּא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הִנֵּה ה֗וּא בֵּ֛ית מָכִ֥יר בֶּן עַמִּיאֵ֖ל בְּל֥וֹ דְבָֽר

verses.restored: King David sent and took him from house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.

familiar.text: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lodebar.

modern.text: So King David had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּקָּחֵ֗הוּ מִבֵּ֛ית מָכִ֥יר בֶּן עַמִּיאֵ֖ל מִלּ֥וֹ דְבָֽר

verses.restored: Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul came to David, fell on his face, and bowed. David said, Mephibosheth. He said, Look, your servant.

familiar.text: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come unto David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!

modern.text: And when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in reverence. Then David said, “Mephibosheth!” “I am your servant,” he replied.

original.text: וַ֠יָּבֹא מְפִיבֹ֨שֶׁת בֶּן יְהוֹנָתָ֤ן בֶּן שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל פָּנָ֖יו וַיִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ מְפִיבֹ֔שֶׁת וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: David said to him, Do not fear. I will surely do covenant-kindness with you for sake of Jonathan your father. I will restore to you all land of Saul your grandfather, and you shall eat bread at my table continually.

familiar.text: And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

modern.text: “Do not be afraid,” said David, “for surely I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ דָוִ֜ד אַל תִּירָ֗א כִּ֣י עָשֹׂה֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה עִמְּךָ֥ חֶ֨סֶד֙ בַּֽעֲבוּר֙ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן אָבִ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֣י לְךָ֔ אֶֽת כָּל שְׂדֵ֖ה שָׁא֣וּל אָבִ֑יךָ וְאַתָּ֗ה תֹּ֥אכַל לֶ֛חֶם עַל שֻׁלְחָנִ֖י תָּמִֽיד

verses.restored: He bowed and said, What is your servant, that you turn toward a dead dog like me?

familiar.text: And he bowed himself, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I am?

modern.text: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog like me?”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁתַּ֕חוּ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֣י פָנִ֔יתָ אֶל הַכֶּ֥לֶב הַמֵּ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּמֽוֹנִי

verses.restored: King called Ziba, servant of Saul, and said, All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to son of your master.

familiar.text: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said unto him, I have given unto thy master’s son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.

modern.text: Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba and said to him, “I have given to your master’s grandson all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶל צִיבָ֛א נַ֥עַר שָׁא֖וּל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֑יו כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה לְשָׁאוּל֙ וּלְכָל בֵּית֔וֹ נָתַ֖תִּי לְבֶן אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: You, your sons, and your servants shall work land for him and bring produce, so son of your master has bread. Yet Mephibosheth son of your master shall eat continually at my table. Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

familiar.text: Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in the fruits, that thy master’s son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master’s son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

modern.text: You and your sons and servants are to work the ground for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master’s grandson may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master’s grandson, is always to eat at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

original.text: וְעָבַ֣דְתָּ לּ֣וֹ אֶֽת הָאֲדָמָ֡ה אַתָּה֩ וּבָנֶ֨יךָ וַעֲבָדֶ֜יךָ וְהֵבֵ֗אתָ וְהָיָ֨ה לְבֶן אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ לֶּ֨חֶם֙ וַאֲכָל֔וֹ וּמְפִיבֹ֨שֶׁת֙ בֶּן אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ יֹאכַ֥ל תָּמִ֛יד לֶ֖חֶם עַל שֻׁלְחָנִ֑י וּלְצִיבָ֗א חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר בָּנִ֖ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים עֲבָדִֽים

verses.restored: Ziba said to king, According to all that my lord king commands his servant, so your servant will do. Mephibosheth shall eat at my table like one of sons of king.

familiar.text: Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king’s sons.

modern.text: And Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do all that my lord the king has commanded.” So Mephibosheth ate at David’s table like one of the king’s own sons.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצַוֶּ֜ה אֲדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת עַבְדּ֔וֹ כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וּמְפִיבֹ֗שֶׁת אֹכֵל֙ עַל שֻׁלְחָנִ֔י כְּאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica. All who lived in Ziba's house became servants of Mephibosheth.

familiar.text: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Micha. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth.

modern.text: And Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.

original.text: וְלִמְפִיבֹ֥שֶׁת בֵּן קָטָ֖ן וּשְׁמ֣וֹ מִיכָ֑א וְכֹל֙ מוֹשַׁ֣ב בֵּית צִיבָ֔א עֲבָדִ֖ים לִמְפִיבֹֽשֶׁת

verses.restored: Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he ate continually at table of king. He was injured in both feet.

familiar.text: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king’s table; and was lame on both his feet.

modern.text: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king’s table, and he was lame in both feet.

original.text: וּמְפִיבֹ֗שֶׁת יֹשֵׁב֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֣י עַל שֻׁלְחַ֥ן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ תָּמִ֖יד ה֣וּא אֹכֵ֑ל וְה֥וּא פִסֵּ֖חַ שְׁתֵּ֥י רַגְלָֽיו

translation_notes: Mephibosheth's disability is descriptive, not punishment, tragedy shorthand, moral defect, or reason for self-contempt.
His fear before David reflects dynastic danger: new kings often eliminated surviving rival households. 'Do not fear' occurs inside a real power imbalance.
Restored land and table access may express covenant-kindness, but continual residence at the royal table may also function as surveillance or political containment.
Mephibosheth's 'dead dog' language reflects hierarchy and vulnerability, not his actual worth.
Ziba's fifteen sons and twenty servants are assigned agricultural labor by royal command. Their work and consent must not disappear beneath the kindness narrative.
Mephibosheth has a son and a continuing family line; disability does not erase sexuality, parenthood, inheritance, competence, or adulthood.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter for disability pity, inspiration stereotypes, forced gratitude, or claims that powerful patrons own disabled people's loyalty. Covenant care should restore resources and dignity without surveillance, coerced dependence, or unpaid labor.
